messages:
maria: Heads up — our blackbox streaming probe in eu-west1 (inference-stream-check) started showing intermittent 503s and websocket closes for GPU-backed pods ~14:05 UTC. Looks correlated with longer streams (>1k tokens).

probe-bot: [probe id=stream-euwest-2] 503 on /v1/stream, 10 failures in last 12m, sample payload size=1.2MB, node=gpu-pool-7b-3. Logs: 
```
websocket: close 1006 (abnormal closure): write tcp 10.12.4.23:45678->10.34.9.12:443: write: connection reset by peer
ERR: upstream write failed: broken pipe
```

samir: I see the same in the probe aggregate: p95 latency spikes before the 503s. This is only on nodes labeled gpu=true, not on cpu pools.

kai: GPU nodes recently got the 525.85 driver update last week — possible nv driver interaction with long-lived websockets? Not sure but worth ruling out.

ingrid: @maria can you paste the PromQL you used? want to check network errors vs pod restarts.

maria: PromQL I used: `sum(rate(probe_http_status{job="blackbox",probe="inference-stream-check",region="eu-west1"}[5m])) by (status)` — shows a jump in 5xx around 14:03. Also `sum by(node) (increase(container_restart_count[30m]))` is flat.

samir: another useful one: `sum(rate(node_network_receive_errs_total[5m])) by (instance)` — no obvious NIC errors. But `node_sockstat_TCP_InUse` on the gpu nodes is higher than normal.

dino: More load from KV cache warmups? streaming tests do heavier KV churn. If the runtime keeps reconnecting it could flood ephemeral ports. Are we seeing SNAT port exhaustion?

maria: checked NAT metrics — ephemeral port usage for the cluster is high but not exhausted.

kai: still could be kernel-level connection drops under high socket churn. Quick test: can we drain one affected gpu node and keep traffic on others? If the failure follows the node we know it's node-local.

samir: I ran a quick grep of the runtime logs on gpu-pool-7b-3:
```
2026-11-02T14:02:59Z [runtime] stream conn id=abc123: handshake completed
2026-11-02T14:03:12Z [runtime] stream conn id=abc123: write failed: write: connection reset by peer
2026-11-02T14:03:12Z [runtime] stream conn id=abc123: closing conn, err=EOF
```

ingrid: envoy config? maybe keepalive/idle timeouts too short for long streams. envoy's idle_timeout defaults can clip long sessions. Which envoy version on gpu nodes?

kai: Envoy is same for all pools. But the upstream envoy -> runtime path uses different sidecar memory limits on gpu nodes (to save RAM). If sidecar OOMs briefly, that'd cause resets but restart counts were flat.

dino: Cost note — if we start increasing probe timeouts or sampling more, that's additional load and some cost on Dedicated clusters. We should balance detection sensitivity vs churn.

samir: Proposed immediate mitigations:
- increase blackbox streaming probe `handshake_timeout` from 10s -> 25s
- change alerting rule to require 3 consecutive scrape-fail windows (5m windows) before page (reduce noisy flaps)
- sample 20% of stream payloads for deep checks (instead of 100%) to reduce load

maria: sounds good. I can push a probe config change to canary (eu-west1-canary) now.

ingrid: For alert tuning, change in Prometheus rule: from `increase(probe_failures[5m]) > 0` to `increase(probe_failures[15m]) >= 3` and also add `and on(region) (sum by(region) (rate(probe_requests[15m])) > 5)` so tiny blips in low-volume zones don't page.

alerts-bot: Alerting rule proposed: `sum by(region) (increase(blackbox_failures_total{probe="inference-stream-check"}[15m])) >= 3` - will create PR for rule-change.

maria: rolling canary applied: updated handshake_timeout -> 25s, sampling -> 20% (deep). Waiting 10m to observe.

probe-bot: after change: 3 failures -> 1 failure in the 10m window on gpu-pool-7b-3, p95 latency still slightly elevated.

samir: if probes calm down we still need a follow-up: drain one gpu node during maintenance window and repro with long streams locally. Also collect `ss -s` and `netstat -anp` before/after.

kai: Agree. I'll coordinate a rolling drain of 1 node in eu-west1 tomorrow 02:00 UTC. Plan: cordon + drain + restart runtime pod + uncordon. If failures persist after restart then escalate to infra for driver/kernel rollback.

dino: FYI: if we back off probe frequency on Dedicated clusters we'll save ~4% of egress CPU cycles on that pool; put that in the change request.

maria: action items:
- (maria) monitor canary config for 1h and post results here
- (samir) create runbook checklist for drain + repro + required logs (`ss -t -a -p`, `/var/log/kern.log`, runtime logs)
- (kai) schedule node drain tomorrow 02:00 UTC and be on-call during it
- (ingrid) open PR to adjust Prometheus rule (alerts-bot started PR)

samir: quick command snippets I'll add to runbook:
```
# collect socket stats
kubectl debug node/gpu-pool-7b-3 -it --image=busybox -- bash -c "ss -s; ss -t -a -o state established"
# check kernel drops
kubectl exec -n infra node-exporter-xyz -- cat /var/log/kern.log | tail -n 200
# collect envoy stats for pod
kubectl exec -n runtime runtime-pod-123 -- curl -s http://127.0.0.1:9901/stats | grep stream
```

maria: thanks all. so far probe noise reduced. will report back after full 1h observation. :thumbsup:

samir: if it comes back, we may need to change the probe logic to do an application-layer keepalive (ping frames) rather than relying on TCP keepalive. That will reduce false positives.

kai: noted. thanks.

probe-bot: updated probe config rolled to eu-west1-canary at 14:25 UTC by maria.

maria: closing loop — 1h in canary looks stable. scheduling the node drain tomorrow to be safe. Will update runbook PR with logs post-drain.

ingrid: great. leaving the alert rule PR open for review. :eyes:
